content: Patient Care Teams are defined as groups of healthcare professionals from various disciplines who collaborate under the leadership of a physician to provide comprehensive care for patients. Each team member has specific roles and responsibilities, and their collective efforts contribute to the overall management and treatment of the patient. The rationale for implementing multidisciplinary patient care teams in diabetes management is supported by the complexity and diversity of quality care markers required for diabetic patients. Meeting these goals is challenging, as evidenced by data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Between 2015 and 2018, only 21. A second study during the same period reported a similar success rate of 22. The implementation of patient care teams has demonstrated improved outcomes in diabetes management. This was significantly higher compared to 8.1% of patients receiving usual care. These findings highlight the effectiveness of patient care teams in improving outcomes for individuals with complex health conditions. However, the success rates in this study were lower than those reported in a prior study conducted by Kaiser. The impact of patient care teams, along with other quality improvement initiatives, has been systematically reviewed to assess their role in enhancing diabetes care.
